meaningful_difference.rationale: Both mappings import the same provenance instrument, but they choose different provenance objects. B tracks BD and O1 as whole documents, which coincides closely with the baseline reporter's ordinary chain-of-custody tracing. A redefines the tracked object as the exact wording of clause K, giving the clause its own custody and copying history separate from any document, and treats authorship and common-origin links as explicit provenance gaps. That is a material difference in what is represented, observed and inferred.

action.rationale: A's practitioner follows the K wording across all six records including the memo p6 and the generic P0 wording, building a clause chronology rather than a document chronology. B's practitioner cross-checks receipts, editing logs and public registration for two whole documents, which is what the baseline reporter already does when tracing document provenance.

observables.rationale: In A the meaningful evidence becomes clause-transmission links (wording appearing, being inserted, being paraphrased) and their compatibility or conflict, distinct from who held a file. In B the evidence remains dated document possession links, which is ordinary evidence for the baseline; B's refusal to equate clause with document is a caution, not a new evidence class.

inferential_warrant.rationale: A warrants conclusions from compatible clause-level links that can be supported beyond, or independently of, whole-document possession, while explicitly withholding origin uniqueness from identical wording. B's warrant is that dated possession bounds who could have had the document before publication, a warrant the baseline reporter already uses.

problem_decomposition.rationale: A splits the case into a clause history and a document history and adds authorship and common-origin links as named unresolved parts, which makes p5 and p6 structural elements rather than side notes. B's decomposition is document-by-document custody plus gap marking, matching the baseline's dated event sequence.

inquiry_trajectory.rationale: A's follow-up is directed by the clause object: check generic P0 wording as a possible common origin and preserve the unstated authorship in p6. B's follow-up marks missing document links and compares P0, a similar move but at document granularity, so it departs less from what the reporter would investigate next anyway.

local_depth.rationale: A's deepest change is re-identifying the provenance object as a clause with its own custody, a representational shift. B's deepest change is applying formal gap-marking to document custody, which is shallow relative to ordinary practice.

inquiry_propagation.rationale: Within the stipulated budget, A's clause framing governs the primary pass over p1-p6 and the follow-up on P0 and p6 authorship. B's document framing governs the primary pass over p1-p4 mainly, with the follow-up reverting to ordinary gap listing.

task_reach.rationale: The steering question turns on how clause K moved from a bidder draft into a requirement competitors failed. A's clause-level reasoning governs that link and the unresolved authorship and common-origin portions. B's document-possession bound addresses advance access but leaves the clause mechanism to ordinary reasoning.

native_reducibility.rationale: B translates back almost losslessly into ordinary chain-of-custody reporting. A's distinction between clause custody and document custody, and its treatment of identical wording as non-unique origin evidence, would be lost if reduced to 'the official had the bidder draft, so the clause came from it'.

decisive_basis.most_important_difference: A changes the unit of provenance from the document to the exact clause wording, while B keeps the ordinary document unit.
decisive_basis.local_depth: A departs more deeply at its most changed point because it re-represents what is being traced; B's most changed point is procedural gap-marking that the baseline already performs informally.
decisive_basis.inquiry_propagation: A's clause framing carries through the primary operation and the follow-up on P0 and p6; B's framing carries through the primary pass but its follow-up is ordinary gap listing.
decisive_basis.task_reach: A's altered reasoning covers the clause-insertion mechanism that decides the steering question and names the unresolved authorship and common-origin parts; B's reasoning covers only pre-publication possession.
decisive_basis.native_reducibility: A is harder to reduce because collapsing clause custody into document custody loses the distinction that identical wording does not fix origin; B is essentially native practice.
decisive_basis.rationale: B has no countervailing displacement advantage. Its explicit refusal to treat clause identity as document identity is a restraint within ordinary practice, not a new mode of inquiry. A's re-identification of the provenance object drives every criterion and every diagnostic in the same direction, so A dominates without needing to weigh opposing edges.

uncertainty: Prospective stage: no realized results, so whether clause-level links actually diverge from document-level links in this world is unknown.
If experienced procurement reporters routinely treat verbatim wording as its own traced object, A's displacement over the baseline would be smaller than assessed.
Budget consumption is unspecified; either branch may use fewer record accesses than assumed.
